SEC10A-14.note: Two independent clauses; semicolon. A splice, C run-on, D 'when' leaves a fragment after the semicolon. Requires locating 'showed' as the second clause's verb. PHASE 2: Explanation correctly identifies the that-clause subject and the D fragment; author 'hard' label is generous, medium.

SEC10A-15.note: Semicolon then fronted participial phrase modifying 'the great fig'. C 'though stripped' is a reduced adverbial, not a conjunction, so it is still a comma splice; C is the strong lure. PHASE 2: Explanation handles the 'though stripped' lure correctly; genuine hard item.

SEC10A-03.note: Long subject 'The decision ... manufacturer' needs a finite main verb; A, C, D all leave the subject without a predicate. B is the only unpunctuated option, which is a mild visual tell. PHASE 2: Explanation sound; the only unpunctuated option being the key is a mild tell, medium not hard.

SEC10A-16.note: Close the parenthetical, no comma between subject and verb. D leaves the parenthesis unclosed (free strike once the '(' is seen); C has no main verb. PHASE 2: Explanation sound; unclosed-paren option is a free strike, so this is easy despite the 'hard' label.

SEC10A-17.note: The 'although' clause has no main clause after it, so it must attach to the preceding independent clause with a comma; A, B, D strand it as a fragment. Counterintuitive for students who reflexively prefer the period. PHASE 2: Explanation sound; good hard item.

SEC10A-18.note: Series of three noun phrases (depth, salinity, date) needs commas; colon and semicolon break the series, no punctuation fuses items. Long first item with embedded clause adds some difficulty. PHASE 2: Explanation sound, including the semicolon-series rule; medium.

SEC10A-07.note: Two independent clauses; period with 'By then' as an introductory phrase. B 'which' relative clause has no gap ('funding' fills the object), A/C are splices. PHASE 2: Explanation sound, including the gapless 'which' in B.

SEC10A-19.note: Summative appositive 'a decision that ...' after a comma. A and B leave 'A decision that ... protested' as a fragment; C is a splice. PHASE 2: Explanation sound.

SEC10A-20.note: Heavy-NP shift: direct object 'three layers' follows the prepositional phrase; no punctuation between verb phrase and its object. Students tend to want a comma; genuinely hard. PHASE 2: Explanation sound; good hard item.

SEC10A-21.note: Nonrestrictive appositive naming 'the only member'; closing comma doubles as the comma before 'and'. D adds a second 'and' (free strike on reading the continuation). PHASE 2: Explanation sound.

SEC10A-22.note: Comma + 'and' joins the two clauses, the 'when' clause is introductory to the second. A reads as a relative 'when' modifying 1927 but then splices onto 'farmers ... found'; strong lure. PHASE 2: Explanation sound; good hard item.

SEC10A-12.note: Colon after an independent clause introduces the explanation 'the royal cubit, a bronze rod ...'. D is a fragment (participles 'kept'/'copied' only), B has no verb, A fuses. PHASE 2: Explanation sound.

SEC10A-13.note: Introductory prepositional phrase then comma. B splits 'negotiations ... over water rights'; C uses a lone dash; D fragment before semicolon. Single dash is a near-free strike. PHASE 2: Explanation sound; easy, mislabelled hard. Ship but relabel.

SEC10B-01.note: Subject 'the network' singular despite intervening 'they form'; A (participle) cannot be the verb of the that-clause. PHASE 2: Explanation sound; medium.

SEC10B-02.note: Comma-set participial phrase of result. Finite forms create a splice / fragment. Easy. PHASE 2: Explanation sound; easy, mislabelled hard. Ship only on an easy/medium route.

SEC10B-03.note: Past tense for a sixteenth-century navigator; A and B are non-finite / doubled relative (free strikes), D present tense contradicts context. PHASE 2: Explanation sound; easy, mislabelled hard (two non-finite options struck freely).

SEC10B-04.note: Two ornithologists, one shared log: plural possessive, singular noun, confirmed by 'it now shows'. Options form a clean 2x2. PHASE 2: Explanation sound.

SEC10B-06.note: Antecedent 'charts' plural; separated from pronoun by a relative clause with 'century' as attractor for 'its'. PHASE 2: Explanation sound.

SEC10B-07.note: Parallel with 'flattens'. Easy. PHASE 2: Explanation sound; easy, mislabelled hard.

SEC10B-08.note: Gerund subject singular, present perfect matches 'now avoid'. B lures with 'wolves'/'years'; D past perfect lacks a past reference point. PHASE 2: Explanation sound, including the past-perfect rejection.

SEC10B-10.note: 'panels' plural immediately before the blank; the long fresco clause is the only distraction. B and D are non-finite/relative fragments. PHASE 2: Explanation sound; easy, the plural head noun sits right next to the blank. Mislabelled hard.

SEC10B-12.note: 'The number of' takes singular. Classic, well-known item type. PHASE 2: Explanation sound; textbook 'the number of', medium at most.

SEC10B-13.note: Compound subject joined by 'and' takes plural; 'combined' semantically needs two things. Singular attractors 'drought'/'pine'. PHASE 2: Explanation sound.

SEC10B-14.note: Dangling modifier: the robe was woven. Each distractor names a different subject; only B can be 'woven'. PHASE 2: Explanation sound; easy-to-medium dangling modifier, mislabelled hard.

SEC10B-15.note: Subject 'source' singular; attractors 'farms', 'bluffs'. C and D add relatives that leave no main verb. PHASE 2: Explanation sound.

SEC10B-16.note: 'person ... who' singular present (he is alive, 'is a farmer'). B non-finite; C past contradicts present situation. PHASE 2: Explanation sound; easy, mislabelled hard.
